mainEntity.name: Can functional medicine help chronic fatigue?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We treat fatigue by addressing what is draining you, the stress response, thyroid, blood sugar, and nutrients, rather than calling it stress. Most people feel steadier energy return as the root causes are corrected.

mainEntity.name: Is adrenal fatigue a real diagnosis?

acceptedAnswer.text: The pattern is real even if the label is debated. What we measure is your cortisol rhythm and how your stress system, thyroid, and metabolism are coping, then we support them directly.

mainEntity.name: What testing do you run for low energy?

acceptedAnswer.text: We go beyond a basic panel, with cortisol rhythm, full thyroid, blood sugar, iron, B12, and vitamin D, so the plan targets your specific root causes.

mainEntity.name: Why am I tired if my doctor says I am fine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard labs flag disease, not how well you function. We read your results against optimal ranges and look at the systems that produce energy, which is where the answer usually hides.

mainEntity.name: How soon will I feel more energy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many people feel a first lift within a few weeks, though deeper recovery follows your body, not a calendar. We pace the plan so progress holds.

mainEntity.name: Can stress really cause physical exhaustion?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A stress response stuck in the on position disrupts sleep, blood sugar, and hormones, and the result is a body that cannot make steady energy. We calm it at the root.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer virtual fatigue care or only in person in Atlanta?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. See Dr. Nina Ross in person at our Atlanta clinic, or virtually anywhere in Georgia. Your $99 Symptom Consultation can be booked either way.

sections.label: Hero

headings.text: Root-cause fatigue care in Atlanta that finally gives you your energy back.

paragraphs: If you wake up tired, run on caffeine, crash by mid afternoon and still cannot fall asleep at night, you are not imagining it.

Your exhaustion is real, and it deserves someone who will listen to the whole story. At Nina Ross Functional Medicine, we treat fatigue at its root, here in Atlanta and virtually across Georgia. Dr. Nina Ross follows the whole picture, the stress response, thyroid, and blood sugar, until she finds what is really draining you, then builds the plan around your body and your life.

sections.label: Why conventional care misses it

headings.text: Your labs were normal, so you were sent home.

eyebrowSpans: Why conventional care keeps missing it
paragraphs: A fifteen-minute visit rarely has room to look at the whole energy system. So fatigue gets brushed off as stress or aging, and the thing draining you goes unexamined.

boldPairs.title: What you’re usually told
boldPairs.body: “Everything looks normal. You are probably just stressed, try to sleep more.”

boldPairs.title: What’s actually happening
boldPairs.body: Cortisol, thyroid, and blood sugar are pulling each other down in a loop. Steady the loop and your energy returns together.

sections.label: The functional medicine difference

headings.text: We will not call it stress and send you home.

paragraphs: Here is where we part ways with conventional care. When the standard panel looks normal, fatigue often gets labeled stress, and you are handed reassurance or a prescription for sleep. That can blunt the feeling for a night. But masking exhaustion does not restore energy. The moment the prescription wears off, the depletion is still there, and often deeper.
We would rather do the harder, more honest work. We find what is actually draining your energy and we treat that.
If a medication still has a place in your care, that should be your informed choice, made with the full picture in front of you, not a default handed to you in a fifteen minute visit.

boldPairs.title: It names a feeling, not a cause
boldPairs.body: Being told you are stressed does not explain why your body stopped making steady energy.

boldPairs.title: A sleep aid can mask the depletion
boldPairs.body: Sedation is not the same as the deep, restoring sleep your body is missing.

boldPairs.title: It postpones the real recovery
boldPairs.body: Pushing through on caffeine borrows energy you do not have, and the debt keeps growing.

sections.label: The root-cause view

headings.text: Fatigue runs in a loop. We map the whole circle.

paragraphs: Each driver pushes the next. That is why treating one in isolation rarely holds, and why mapping the full cycle changes everything.
When we investigate your fatigue, we read the whole stress and metabolic picture rather than a single number, and connect each driver back to what you’re feeling:

strongBullets.label: Cortisol & the stress response
strongBullets.full: Cortisol & the stress response, the wired-but-tired nights and the flat, heavy mornings.

strongBullets.label: An underactive thyroid
strongBullets.full: An underactive thyroid, the slow metabolism, the cold, and the bone-deep tiredness.

strongBullets.label: Blood sugar swings
strongBullets.full: Blood sugar swings, behind the mid-afternoon crash and the cravings that follow.

strongBullets.label: Nutrient depletion
strongBullets.full: Nutrient depletion, low iron, B12, or vitamin D quietly draining your reserves.

strongBullets.label: Unrefreshing sleep
strongBullets.full: Unrefreshing sleep, hours in bed that never add up to real recovery.

strongBullets.label: Mitochondrial strain
strongBullets.full: Mitochondrial strain, where your cells struggle to turn food into steady energy.

strongBullets.label: Chronic inflammation
strongBullets.full: Chronic inflammation, the low hum that keeps your body from ever feeling rested.
